title: Compliance Chronicle: Collector for Residency/Retention Artifacts and Proof Index
creator: Priya Menon
description: Implement a centralized collector and immutable index ("Proof Index") that automates capture and retention of artifacts required for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 controls tied to data residency and retention policies. This ticket covers product requirements, collection adapters, retention lifecycle hooks, proof-index schema, and a minimal search/lookup API to support audits. The goal is to reduce manual auditor work by surfacing curated, tamper-evident bundles mapped to specific control assertions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Collector plugins for S3 (region-tagged), DB export snapshots, and Console audit logs available and validated in staging; 2) Proof Index stores immutable references with at-rest checksum and region metadata; 3) UI or API can assemble an evidence bundle for a chosen control and time window within 30s; 4) Retention policies applied automatically when bundle TTL expires and retention tombstones recorded; 5) Automated test that simulates auditor retrieval and verifies chain-of-custody headers.
proposed_solution:
- Define a minimal Proof Index schema (id, control_refs, artifact_refs, region, retention_policy_id, created_by, created_at, checksum).
- Build collector adapters that normalize artifact metadata and push verifiable records to the Proof Index service.
- Integrate with existing retention scheduler (or extend if missing) so bundles respect jurisdictional TTLs.
- Add a search endpoint and an 'export vault' that packages artifacts with signed manifest for auditor download.
- Add RBAC gating for who can request or consume bundles.
- Start with 3 adapters (S3, Postgres snapshot manifest, Console audit log exporter) and iterate.
success_metrics: - Time to assemble evidence bundle <= 30s for 95th percentile; - Manual auditor time reduced by 60% in pilot; - Number of audit requests served automatically in pilot >= 5; - False-positive/missing-artifact rate < 2% in automated tests.
